newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU gives go-ahead for info technology talks.
newsitem.headline: EU gives go-ahead for info technology talks.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers gave the European Commission the go-ahead on Monday to negotiate a global information technology agreement (ITA) on their behalf, a Commission spokesman told reporters.
"The ITA mandate went through," the spokesman said on the margins of a regular meeting of EU foreign affairs ministers. He declined to give further detail.

The agreement allows the Commission to continue on a more formal basis its work on negotiations with trading partners such as the United States and Japan on a planned liberalisation pact affecting an estimated $400 billion in trade.

Participating countries would agree to eliminate all tariffs on a range of electronic products by 2000, a move affecting duties on computer hardware and software, semi-conductors, facsimile machines and other telecommunications products which would be gradually repealed from next year.
Tariffs would be taken to zero by the end of the century on a most-favoured-nation (MFN) basis.

ITA negotiations hit a snag earlier this year when the EU refused to discuss the accord, complaining that its exclusion from a U.S.-Japanese semiconductor deal signed in July would block European access to Japan's computer-chip market.
The United States and Japan have eliminated tariffs on semiconductors, while EU member states maintain an average tariff of seven percent.

Member countries of the 18-nation Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum remain to be convinced about the tariff phase-out plan, with many of them unwilling to commit to a single date for tariff phase-out which they say would favour countries with the largest existing market shares.
